passages.latin_short: reverso Sole ad eandem horam aequalem natalis
passages.normalized_english: The Sun returns to the same equal natal hour on successive following days; successive days correspond to years.
passages.finding: supports postnatal-day year matching; no modern TT/UT or exact continuous fractional-day interpolation specified.

passages.latin_short: Duplex est motus Directionis, Directus ... & conversus
passages.normalized_english: Distinguishes direct and converse motions; converse is toward preceding places.
passages.finding: converse is source-defined motion, not proof of our generic 360-minus-arc model.

passages.latin_short: motu converso non possunt dirigi Cardines
passages.normalized_english: Angles cannot be directed in converse motion.
passages.finding: explicit exclusion of moving natal angles in Placidus 1657.

passages.latin_short: motu vero converso radios tantum, & Parallelos in mundo, & nullo modo in zodiaco
passages.normalized_english: Under converse, planetary significators receive rays and parallels in mundo, not zodiacal rays.
passages.finding: original Latin independently confirms Cooper 1814's restriction.

passages.latin_short: in Directione conversa locum non habent radij in zodiaco
passages.normalized_english: Reiterates that zodiacal rays have no place in converse.

passages.latin_short: ad primum annum post natalem accipimus partem illam aequatoris, quam ascendit Sol in sphaera recta motu primae diei post natalem
passages.normalized_english: For first year, take equatorial arc ascended by Sun in first day after birth; second year's equatorial interval comes from second subsequent day, etc.
passages.finding: source supports successively accumulated solar right ascension, rather than a universal fixed Naibod constant.

passages.canon: Canon de directionibus ad familiaritates in zodiaco
passages.latin_short: in motu Directionis converso ... significator manet immobilis sub Primo Mobile, sed movetur motu universali raptus
passages.normalized_english: In converse Placidus describes a significator fixed relative to primum mobile, moving with its universal rotation toward fixed promissor in worldly configuration.
passages.finding: source-defined role relations need careful reference-frame interpretation; do not automatically equate source text with our generic program's role-swapped geometry without full canon checking.

comparator.edition: John Cooper edited English Primum Mobile, London 1814

correspondences.assessment: agrees on prohibition of angles in converse
agrees on prohibition of zodiacal rays in converse
agrees on converse as mundane-only for rays
agrees on varying successive-day equatorial solar arc as year measure
